walkthroughs.body_html:
UK in the 21st Century — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

UK in the 21st Century brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with UK in the 21st Century.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: The San Andreas Fault is what type of margin?
options: Constructive
Destructive
Conservative
Collision

mcqs.q: Why do TNCs locate production in LICs?
options: Plates move because of ocean tides pulling on the crust.
Because LICs have better infrastructure than HICs.
Because TNCs want to develop poorer countries and lift them out of poverty.
Lower labour costs, weaker regulation, access to raw materials, large potential markets, and government incentives like tax breaks in special economic zones.

mcqs.q: What drives the movement of tectonic plates?
options: Plates move because of ocean tides pulling on the crust.
Abrasion is when wind erodes the glacier and plucking is when rain does.
The Earth's rotation makes the plates move.
Convection currents in the mantle combined with slab pull at subduction zones and ridge push at constructive boundaries.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between glacial abrasion and plucking?
options: Abrasion is when wind erodes the glacier and plucking is when rain does.
Abrasion and plucking are different words for the same process.
Because LICs have better infrastructure than HICs.
Abrasion: rock embedded in the glacier base scrapes the bedrock smooth, creating striations. Plucking: meltwater refreezes onto bedrock, then movement rips chunks of rock away.
